items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: Alice,oh, what's her name, the Whitman sisters, they were there all the time.

ctx.x: My People. It was the education of the Negro through music. And he developed it and oh, it was beautiful and the last thing was 'What is Color? What is Virtue?' He developed that thing, he was working over in Detroit and he come over and fix a part and go back to the show, to his show, when we was in Detroit. That lasted -- we'd go on -- and I'd have to go out in the lobby and I said tell the band leader, don't go until I tell you, because the people are lined out there coming into the show. They would come there

two and three times a week to see that show. Butterbeans and Susie they were there looked like every day and Alice,oh, what's her name, the Whitman sisters, they were there all the time. That was a great show.
You'd have three and four thousand people at that show.
